main_text.p: omnes per Bosphorum navigantes, ab-stinere armis coëgerunt. Eodemque tempore pecuniâ & rebus bello gerendo necessariis Synopenses obsecrantes juverunt. Posteà cum Romani rebus Græciæ & Asiæ contra Philippum Macedonem, & Antiochum Magnum Syriæ regem miscere se cœpislent, contra utrumque Romanis adhæsére, & perutilem iis operam præstitére, cum mari præ reliquis Græci nominis populis plurimum eâ ætate valerent. Itaque magnis quoque honoribus ac præmiis, partâ contra utrumque victoriâ, inprimis verò Antiocho superato, & trans Taurum montem ex Asiâ citeriore submoto, sunt affecti, magnâ Lyciæ & Cariæ parte donati, socii & amici populi Romani appellati. Hoc verò maximè laudabile, quòd cum de præmiis Eumenis regis amicissimi Romæ in curiâ age-retur, pro libertate civitatum Græcarum, quæ Eumenis novis finibus con-tinebantur, non veriti regem amicum & vicinum offendere, enixè laborarint. Manifestum enim faciebant, non sui tantum rationem se habere, sed toti genti Græcæ cupere quàm optimè. page.notes: Show-through from the reverse page at the left edge ("reg", "gnis", fragments of lines) and small marks at lower left ("8", "9") are not printed text on this page and were left out. "dera" at lower right is the catchword. The line "age-retur" follows the printed hyphenation as it appears; the reading "agebatur" was not confirmed letter by letter. Long s has been transcribed as plain s throughout, as instructed. The paragraph division at the top is not clear from the scan, so the page is given as one paragraph continuing from the previous page.
